newsitem.title: INDIA: India Marxist says oil price hike debate on Monday.
newsitem.headline: India Marxist says oil price hike debate on Monday.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition will meet on Monday to thrash out the politically sensitive issue of an increase in the prices of oil products, the country's main Marxist party said.

Jyoti Basu, whose Communist Party of India (Marxist) or CPI(M) is the second-largest partner in the United Front, told Reuters in an interview late on Saturday that the coalition's policy-making Steering Committee would meet in New Delhi on Monday.
Coalition officials have said the Steering Committee is likely to meet at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT) on Monday to take up the issue. The meeting had been scheduled for Sunday but was postponed.
"We have given an alternative document to the Steering Committee," said Basu, who is the chief minister of West Bengal state.

The CPI(M)'s plan, which seeks to avoid what it views as a crippling rise in oil product prices, has called for the federal government to return to the state-run oil sector surplus funds taken from it by earlier governments, and the elimination of customs and excise duties.

On Sunday the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Laloo Prasad Yadav, chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar and a member of the Steering Committee, as saying that he supported a "reasonable hike" in petroleum product prices.
"The hike should be reasonable, which should not cause hardship to the people," PTI quoted Yadav as saying.
Yadav is also the president of the Janata Dal, the largest member of the 15-party coalition government.
Basu said he was travelling to New Delhi on Sunday for the crucial meeting. The Steering Committee has met twice before but failed to reach a consensus on the oil issue.

"There we shall discuss whether our alternative is acceptable or it has to be changed a bit, or whether they think we have to go the whole hog with what some of the other parties are saying," Basu said, referring to demands by other coalition partners for a sharp increase in prices of some oil products.
Any increase in prices this week would be the second by the United Front coalition in its one year in power.

Last July the government raised the price of gasoline by 25 percent, and prices of high-speed diesel, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for cooking, paraffin wax and fuel oil by 30 percent. It was forced to scale back the rise in diesel prices to 15 percent after nationwide protests.

"This has a history. We have to bear the sins of the previous Congress government. For two-and-a-half years when they were there they did not make any changes," Basu added. "Let us see now whether the alternative will work."
Basu was referring to the previous Congress government's only increase, in the prices of gasoline and diesel, in February 1994.

Domestic oil firms were owed 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March from the oil pool account deficit, which represents the amount owed by the government to the companies for selling below market prices.
